questions.question:
For what values of [latex]\alpha[/latex] and [latex]\beta[/latex]
 the following simultaneous equations have an infinite
number of solutions ? x + y + z = 5; x + 3y + 3z = 9; x + 2y + [latex]\alpha[/latex]z = [latex]\beta[/latex]
questions.explanation: The augmented matrix for this system is, [latex]\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 &1 \\ 1& 3 & 3\\ 1 & 2 & \alpha \end{matrix}\right| \begin{matrix} 5\\ 9\\ \beta \end{matrix}\right ][/latex] Using Gauss-elimination method we get [latex]\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 &1 \\ 1& 3 & 3\\ 1 & 2 & \alpha \end{matrix}\right| \begin{matrix} 5\\ 9\\ \beta \end{matrix}\right ]\xrightarrow[R_{3}-R_{1}]{\overset{R_{2}-R_{1}}{\rightarrow}}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 & 1\\ 0 & 2 & 2\\ 0 & 1 & \alpha -1 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 5\\ 4\\ \beta -5 \end{matrix} \right ]\xrightarrow[]{R_{3}-\frac{1}{2}R_{2}}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 & 1\\ 0 & 2 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & \alpha -2 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 5\\ 4\\ \beta -7 \end{matrix} \right ][/latex] Now, for infinite solution last row must be completely zero i.e. [latex]\alpha -2[/latex] and [latex]\beta -7=0[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow \;\;\; \alpha =2[/latex] and [latex]\beta =7[/latex]

[latex]\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 &1 \\ 1& 3 & 3\\ 1 & 2 & \alpha \end{matrix}\right| \begin{matrix} 5\\ 9\\ \beta \end{matrix}\right ][/latex]
Using Gauss-elimination method we get
[latex]\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 &1 \\ 1& 3 & 3\\ 1 & 2 & \alpha \end{matrix}\right| \begin{matrix} 5\\ 9\\ \beta \end{matrix}\right ]\xrightarrow[R_{3}-R_{1}]{\overset{R_{2}-R_{1}}{\rightarrow}}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 & 1\\ 0 & 2 & 2\\ 0 & 1 & \alpha -1 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 5\\ 4\\ \beta -5 \end{matrix} \right ]\xrightarrow[]{R_{3}-\frac{1}{2}R_{2}}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 1 & 1 & 1\\ 0 & 2 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & \alpha -2 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 5\\ 4\\ \beta -7 \end{matrix} \right ][/latex]

questions.question:
A body originally at [latex]60^{\circ}C[/latex]
 cools down to 40[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C in 15 minutes when kept in air at a temperature 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. What will be the temperature of the body at the end of 30 minutes ?
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned}\frac{d\theta }{dt}&=-K\left ( \theta -\theta _{0} \right )\\ \text{(Newtons law }&\text{of cooling)} \\ \frac{d\theta }{\theta -\theta _{0}}&=-K\, dt \\ \int \frac{d\theta }{\theta -\theta _{0}}&=\int -Kdt \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \ln \left ( \theta -\theta _{0} \right )&=-Kt+C_{1} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \theta -\theta _{0}&=C.e^{-Kt} \\   \theta &=\theta _{0}+C.e^{-Kt}\\ \text{Given, } \theta _{0}&=25^{\circ}C \\ \text{Now at } t&=0,\, \theta =60^{\circ} \\  60&=25+ C.e^{0} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; C&=35 \\ \therefore \;\;  \theta &=25+35e^{-Kt} \\ \text{at } t&=15 \text{ minutes}\\ \theta &=40^{\circ}C \\ \therefore \; 40&=25+35e^{-K\times 15} \\ \Rightarrow \;e^{-15K}&=\frac{3}{7}\\ \text{Now at }t&=30 \text{ minutes}, \\ \theta &=25+35e^{-30K} \\  &=25+35\left ( e^{-15K} \right )^{2} \\  &=25+35\times \left ( \frac{3}{7} \right )^{2} \\    &=31.428^{\circ}C\approx 31.5^{\circ}C \end{aligned}[/latex]
